item.title: One Dead, Three Rescued As Building Collapses In Lagos
item.description: One person has been confirmed dead and three others injured after a building collapsed in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. The incident occurred on Akinola Street, off Ikorodu Road, on Friday morning. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said that while the cause of the collapse has yet to be ascertained, emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (on-site workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. LASEMA said emergency responders have begun a coordinated search of the incident scene to ensure the prompt rescue of victims trapped under the collapsed building. It also noted that it is managing the incident scene to ensure a successful operation in collaboration with stakeholders, including the LRU paramedics, Lagos State Fire Service, LASASA and the Alabama Division of the Nigeria Police Force. item.title: State Police Has Received Approval Of 24 Houses of Assembly, Met Constitutional Threshold — Gbajabiamila
item.description: The Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, has met the threshold of two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly as required by law, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill said on Friday. Chairman of the group and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed in a statement that the bill has been approved by 24 Houses of Assembly. “The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill notes with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states,” it said. “The Working Group commends the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.” Members of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill: (L-R) Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Gbajabiamila; Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, addressing journalists on August 3, 2026. (Photo by Lanre Lasisi/Channels TV) It said that in line with Section 9 of the Constitution, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. item.title: Kanayo, Kate Henshaw, others mourn late actor Francis Duru
item.description: Some Nigerian actors have expressed grief over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru, describing him as a talented performer whose contributions to the film industry would be remembered. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Duru died on Friday at the age of 57 following a brief illness. His passing comes just two years after the tragic loss of his 15-year-old son, Ifeanyi, leaving fans and the film industry in deep mourning. Actor Kanayo O. Kanayo, in a tribute shared on his Instagram page, described Duru as a consummate actor and one of Nigeria’s most versatile and prolific performers. “A consummate actor has left the stage. One of the most flexible, prolific performers Nigeria ever produced. Rest in peace, my brother,” Kanayo wrote. Actress Kate Henshaw also mourned Duru, reflecting on the brevity of life and praying for the repose of his soul. “Like a flame gone out, so are our lives when it all ends,” she wrote, adding a prayer for God to grant Duru eternal rest and comfort his loved ones. Similarly, actress Mercy Johnson-Okojie expressed her grief, saying she was too overwhelmed by the loss to find the words to describe her feelings. “Too tired and speechless about this loss,” she wrote. Actress Stephanie Linus described Duru’s death as tragic and heartbreaking, praying for strength for his family to bear the loss. “Such a tragic and heartbreaking loss. May God grant his family the strength and fortitude to bear this loss. May his soul rest in peace. RIP Francis Duru,” she wrote. The tributes reflect the grief of Duru’s colleagues over the loss of a fellow actor whose performances endeared him to audiences. Duru rose to fame for his role as Ahanna in Amaka Igwe’s classic film Rattlesnake, building a career that spanned more than three decades in the Nigerian film industry. The actor’s family announced his death in a statement on his official Instagram page in the early hours of Oct. 23, 2026. item.title: Kaduna rally: ‘Your posters enjoy protection Nigerians can only dream of’ — Atiku tackles Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Atiku Abubakar, former vice-president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has criticised President Bola Tinubu over reports that security operatives are guarding his campaign billboards in Kaduna State ahead of Saturday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign launch. In a post on X on Friday, Atiku questioned why Tinubu’s campaign posters were seen protected while Nigerians continued to face attacks by bandits and terrorists. “Bola, you claim Nigerians love you, yet your billboards in Kaduna require security guards. Bandits raid villages, terrorists attack communities, and families live in fear. Your posters enjoy protection that millions of Nigerians can only dream of,” he wrote. “What a tragic statement of your government’s priorities. Bola, please protect Nigerians with the same urgency you protect your image!” he added. Tinubu is expected to attend the inaugural APC presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24, alongside other top government officials. Ahead of the visit, the Kaduna State Police Command announced restrictions on trailers, tankers, lorries and other heavy-duty vehicles in Kaduna metropolis from midnight until 8pm on Saturday. The Commissioner of Police, Muhammad Rabiu, said the restriction followed consultations between the state security committee and transport unions and was intended to ease traffic congestion and ensure smooth movement during the presidential visit. Rabiu said the police, military, Department of State Services and other security agencies had put security arrangements in place, including the deployment of tactical teams, explosive ordnance disposal units, traffic officers and crowd-control personnel. He also warned political parties and their supporters against thuggery, violence, intimidation and the possession of dangerous weapons, urging residents to cooperate with security agencies to ensure a peaceful campaign rally. item.title: Netanyahu orders West Bank closure as attack wounds Israelis before election
item.description: Palestinian militants wounded five Israelis in an attack on Friday before being killed in a shootout with soldiers, leading Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order a lockdown in the occupied West Bank days before Israeli elections. Netanyahu, facing a tight race for a new term in Tuesday’s vote, said that Israeli troops prevented what could have been a major attack, with the two assailants allegedly carrying a large quantity of ammunition in their vehicle. Militant group Hamas, without claiming responsibility, praised the attack as a “heroic operation” and called for more. A Hebron-based AFP photographer who was en route to another assignment witnessed the gun battle break out at the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint near the Palestinian city, and saw two Palestinian men armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces. Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers, with the AFP journalist seeing their lifeless bodies on the ground next to a petrol station as troops patrolled all around. The Israeli military said soldiers had rushed to the Judea Junction area after the early-morning shooting and “eliminated two terrorists”. The attack wounded five people, two of whom were in critical condition, said Magen David Adom, Israel’s emergency medical rescue service. The service said all five were Israelis in their 20s, including one man in “very serious condition” with gunshot wounds. With the clock counting down to election day, Netanyahu called for all Likud party political meetings to be cancelled Friday due to the attack. – ‘Full lockdown’ – “I salute the courage of our soldiers who acted with determination and prevented what could have been a major attack,” Netanyahu said in a statement. “I have instructed the IDF (army) and security forces to impose an immediate cordon on the city of Hebron and to prepare for a full lockdown of all of Judea and Samaria starting today,” Netanyahu said, using the biblical name for the Israeli-occupied West Bank. He added that troops were “carrying out stepped-up operations to thwart terrorist activities and are conducting large-scale waves of arrests”. The military said it had “launched offensive counter-terrorism operations in the Hebron area”, adding that troops were raiding homes of the suspects and others. item.title: Pope Leo to miss Assisi gathering – Vatican
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will not attend a peace gathering at Assisi next week on doctors’ advice as he recovers from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said Friday. “To support recovery following last Tuesday’s thoracic surgery, and following the doctors’ advice, Pope Leo XIV will not be able to attend the ‘Disarmed and Disarming Peace’ meeting in Assisi on October 27th,” wrote the Vatican in a note. The Assisi meeting, on the 40th anniversary of the World Day of Prayer for Peace, will go ahead with Leo sending a message to the event, the Vatican said. The doctors, Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora, wrote in a separate note published by the Vatican that although a chest X-ray of the pope showed “excellent progress of the post-operative recovery”, they advised caution for the Assisi trip. “Considering the short time since the surgery, the attending doctors thought it prudent, as a precaution, to advise against the scheduled helicopter trip on October 27,” they said. Leo, 71, was discharged on Saturday from Rome’s Gemelli hospital five days after surgery to remove the lower part of his right lung where they had detected a cancerous nodule. His doctors said Wednesday that no further therapy was required following the successful operation, with the cancer having been found to be “localised”. On Sunday, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics said he would resume his duties “gradually”. Doctors have said there is no medical reason that the pope cannot go ahead with a long-planned visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he lived for two decades, on November 6-17. Leo last visited Assisi — which celebrates this year the 800th anniversary of St Francis’ death — in August for an event with thousands of young people from across Europe. The prayer event, held from October Sunday to Tuesday, will bring together 384 representatives of religions, cultures and institutions from 53 countries, according to the Vatican. item.title: Video: Peter Obi has made Obidients everybody’s enemy — Sowunmi
item.description: Segun Sowunmi, a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has accused former Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi of turning his supporters, popularly known as Obidients, against prominent Nigerians through their criticism of public figures. Sowunmi made the allegation during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub , where he criticised Obi’s political movement and argued that its supporters had become hostile to people who disagreed with them. “The problem with the Igbo agenda Peter Obi is running is that he has made his Obidients to become enemy of everybody,” he said. “Their hand is on everybody’s name. They will abuse Wole Soyinka, they will abuse Okupe. We are not going to relinquish our country to their madness.” Sowunmi’s comments came as political parties and their supporters position themselves ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC chieftain also spoke about regional political influence, arguing that political power must be negotiated and that leaders should protect their interests within their respective areas. Referring to the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, Sowunmi said Nigeria had lost influential figures who previously played important roles in representing their people. “Baba Fasoranti has just gone now. Those are the leaders that used to carry this weight for us,” he said. He questioned whether Yoruba political leaders should surrender their influence while other groups continued to pursue their interests. “You want me to lie on the ground and have some people overrun us?” he asked. Sowunmi argued that political groups should be allowed to shape the direction of politics in their respective regions, adding that the Yoruba should not be expected to abandon their own interests in the name of being reasonable. “You want me to sit down here as a bona fide Yoruba man, to say that okay, because we are reasonable, we will not control the directive principle of our areas?” he said. He maintained that political power required negotiation and said the Yoruba had experience in that process. “Power must be negotiated, and the Yorubas are good at doing that,” Sowunmi added. Obi, who came third in the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, drew considerable support from young Nigerians through the Obidient movement. His supporters have remained a visible force in Nigeria’s political debate, while critics have questioned the tone of some online exchanges involving the movement. item.title: 2027: Adeleke backs Tinubu; maintains support for Accord legislative candidates
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has pledged to mobilise more than 1.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in January 2027, while insisting that his support for Accord Party candidates in legislative elections remains unchanged. Adeleke said a coalition involving the Accord Party, All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) was working together solely to secure Tinubu’s re-election. The governor disclosed this in a post on X on Friday, following the inauguration of the Osun State Presidential Campaign Council for Tinubu’s re-election. “Our rainbow coalition of Accord, APC and PDP is united solely for President Tinubu’s re-election in the January 2027 presidential election. This partnership does not extend to the legislative elections,” he wrote. The governor also provided an update on the Osun local government crisis, saying negotiations were at an advanced stage and that he had received assurances from the federal government. “On the Osun local government crisis, negotiations are at an advanced stage. I have received the assurance of the Federal Government, and there will be positive developments soon,” he said. item.title: US Conference of Catholic Bishops says not linked to Trump prayer event
item.description: The United States Conference of Catholic Bishops on Thursday told AFP it was not linked to a group seen in a video praying with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office. “This was not something that the USCCB organized. It is not affiliated with the Conference. I have no further information,” said a spokesperson for the organization, Chieko Noguchi, to AFP. On Thursday an aide to the US president, Margo Martin, shared a video showing the president seated at his desk, flanked by clergy wearing collars. One had his hand on the president’s shoulder and prayed aloud. “Catholic Archbishops and Bishops pray with President Trump in the Oval Office,” captioned Martin in her post on X, including a heart emoji. The White House later confirmed to AFP that the president had met with a dozen Catholic faith leaders, including the archbishops of Denver, Milwaukee and Kansas City. The Trump administration’s relationship with the Catholic Church has been fraught, particularly regarding the policy of deporting migrants. Trump, who enjoyed support from the Christian right during his most recent presidential campaign, has held several prayer gatherings similar to Thursday’s event, including with evangelical pastors. item.title: South-East has better presidential options than Peter Obi – Umahi
item.description: Nigeria’s Minister of Works, David Umahi, has said Peter Obi is not the best presidential candidate the South-East can produce, arguing that the former Anambra State governor failed to consult regional political leaders before pursuing his 2023 presidential ambition. Umahi made the remarks in an interview with Arise News and insisted his stance on Peter Obi’s candidacy was not driven by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the Southeast has other qualified political figures capable of seeking the presidency. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the political interests of the South-East at the national level should first engage governors and other influential stakeholders in the region to build consensus. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi added that if he were seeking the presidency, he would consult widely with political leaders before declaring his ambition, stressing that such a move should not be undertaken without engaging those whose interests the candidate claims to represent. He also challenged the perception that Obi should automatically be considered the South-East’s strongest presidential option because of his performance in the 2023 election. According to him, the region has several qualified politicians who should be considered in future discussions about producing Nigeria’s president. The minister further argued that the presidency should not automatically be allocated to Anambra State whenever the South-East gets an opportunity to produce a president. He noted that Nigeria’s first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, hailed from the area that now forms Anambra State, adding that Ebonyi, Enugu, Abia and Imo should also be considered. Umahi’s comments came amid growing political discussions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, particularly over support for President Bola Tinubu among political leaders in the South-East. Umahi defended those backing Tinubu, rejecting suggestions that their political choices amounted to a betrayal of the region. He maintained that the South-East could improve its chances of producing a president through negotiations and alliances with other parts of the country rather than treating support for any individual politician as a measure of regional loyalty. item.title: Asian football makes U-turn, endorses Infantino re-election
item.description: The head of Asian football on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president, weeks after stinging criticism over his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The AFC in August had joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term. “I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman. “I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. “I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.” Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past. “But let’s not relate the two things together. item.title: FG to complete records of Nigerian casualties, assets lost during ECOMOG wars
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), has disclosed that efforts are ongoing to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets of the Nigerian military and other personnel who paid the ultimate sacrifice in the ECOMOG operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone, noting that it is aimed at ensuring proper preservation for posterity. Musa reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to immortalising the legacy and sacrifices of the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG). The Minister made the disclosure when he received a delegation of ECOMOG Veterans, led by Major General Ohifeme Ejimai (Rtd), at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Abuja. A statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, SA Media, said the delegation paid the courtesy visit to brief the minister on the group’s activities and ongoing initiatives. General Musa acknowledged the significant human and financial resources Nigeria deployed under ECOMOG, emphasising that personnel who paid the supreme price particularly during peacekeeping missions in Liberia and Sierra Leone will never be forgotten. He assured the delegation that ongoing efforts to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets would be thoroughly completed to ensure proper preservation for posterity. Earlier on his remarks, Major General Ejimai (Rtd) provided an update on the status of surviving Nigerian ECOMOG veterans, noting their readiness to continue contributing to national development and security. He urged the Ministry to address documentation gaps and consider establishing a dedicated remembrance day to honour the hundreds of Nigerian troops who lost their lives to secure peace and stability in West Africa. The Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was a formal regional peacekeeping and peace enforcement force created by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 1990. Driven significantly by Nigerian leadership and troops, ECOMOG played a decisive role in restoring constitutional order, protecting civilian populations, and stabilising West Africa during complex regional crises. item.title: Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism
item.description: Manchester United great Wayne Rooney has labelled the current squad “babies” and “selfish” after a humiliating Champions League capitulation and post-match criticism by Bruno Fernandes of manager Michael Carrick. Carrick’s men are 13th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday’s visit by Bournemouth and could drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend. With the club beset by infighting and off to their worst domestic league start for decades, Carrick was left clinging to his job after the 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday. Deepening the sense of crisis, the captain Fernandes afterwards took aim at his manager’s tactics, saying United had to be more “brave”. Defender Lisandro Martinez last week criticised the club’s board for not investing enough in the transfer market. Rooney, United’s all-time leading goalscorer, said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at the Como display. A friend and ex-teammate of Carrick, former striker Rooney pointed the finger at the players. “When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told The United Stand podcast on Thursday. “That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because these players, they don’t want to take responsibility. “You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.” He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. “If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.” The post Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the Federal Government saying it has intensified efforts to contain Nigeria’s confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease; placed high-risk contacts in quarantine, isolated other contacts and strengthened preparedness across states as well as health facilities. Another headline features the National Economic Council (NEC) endorsing a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms. item.title: Family reputation must not shield child abusers—DSVA
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency (DSVA), Mrs. Titilola Vivour-Adeniyi, has warned families against prioritising their reputation over the protection of children who suffer sexual abuse. Vivour-Adeniyi, who was the chief reviewer of Flora’s Flower, a book written by journalist and child rights advocate, Funmi Ajumobi, said the culture of silence surrounding child sexual abuse often prevented survivors from speaking out and perpetrators from being held accountable. The review highlighted how family pressure, stigma and fear of public embarrassment could discourage parents and guardians from reporting abuse, leaving affected children without the protection and support they need. The book tells the story of Flora, a 16-year-old secondary school student who suffers abuse by people she knows and trusts, and explores how poor communication and silence can allow abuse to continue. Vivour-Adeniyi stressed the need for parents to create safe environments where children could discuss their experiences without fear of blame, intimidation or rejection. The review also cautioned against excessive parental control that isolates children from trusted adults who could recognise signs of abuse and offer help. It urged parents and guardians to take children’s disclosures seriously, report suspected abuse promptly and seek assistance from designated health facilities, trauma centres and relevant authorities. On access to justice, the review noted that prosecuting offenders was not enough, stressing the need for counselling, medical care, psychosocial support and educational reintegration for survivors. It also called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, law enforcement authorities, schools, healthcare providers and civil society organisations to improve child protection and support services. The review further urged schools to provide trained counsellors and clear reporting channels, while encouraging religious institutions and community leaders to challenge the stigma associated with sexual abuse. It stressed that children who experience abuse must not be blamed for the actions of perpetrators, adding that protecting family reputation should never take precedence over a child’s safety and wellbeing. Vivour-Adeniyi also recommended the use of Flora’s Flower in schools, parent forums, religious institutions and community outreach programmes to promote awareness of child protection and encourage the reporting of abuse. item.title: Vanguard a dream, a place where destinies thrive — Ajumobi
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Author of Flora’s Flower, Funmi Ajumobi, has described Vanguard Media Limited as a platform where destinies thrive, talents are nurtured and individuals are empowered to achieve their potential. Ajumobi, who spoke at the public presentation of her book in Lagos, expressed gratitude to Vanguard’s Publisher, Mr Sam Amuka; Chairman, Mrs Omasan Dudu; Editor, Mr Eze Anaba; and the board of editors for their support. “For me, Vanguard is more than a newspaper organisation. Vanguard is a place where destinies are allowed to thrive. It is a place where people are given opportunities to discover their voices, develop their abilities and become more than they initially imagined,” she said. She also appreciated former Lagos State First Lady, Mrs Abimbola Fashola, for encouraging her to rewrite the book after the first manuscript was claimed by another person. Explaining the motivation behind Flora’s Flower, Ajumobi said the book highlights the need to support child abuse survivors beyond the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators. She said society must prioritise survivors’ emotional wellbeing, education, safety and recovery, stressing that justice should not end with punishment. “We must also put the interest, safety, dignity, healing and future of the survivor at the centre of our response,” she said. Ajumobi called for stronger support systems, including counselling, medical care, legal assistance and safe spaces where children could speak without fear. She disclosed that part of the proceeds from the book launch would support a breakfast-feeding initiative for children in Ikorodu, Lagos State, to encourage school attendance and reduce their vulnerability. The author also urged parents, teachers, religious leaders, government agencies and the media to strengthen child protection efforts. She said Flora’s Flower was designed to serve as an educational resource, with child-protection helpline information for different countries to help survivors identify where to seek assistance. item.title: UK, Nigeria deepen collaboration on AI governance, digital transformation
item.description: By Juliet Umeh The United Kingdom and Nigeria have strengthened their collaboration on artificial intelligence governance and digital transformation, following a series of engagements involving the British Standards Institution, BSI, and Nigerian government agencies. The engagements included an Executive Workshop on AI Governance and Standards, delivered by BSI in partnership with the National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, NCAIR, under the UK Government’s Digital Access Programme. The workshop brought together senior government officials, regulators and technology practitioners to examine how internationally recognised standards can support responsible AI adoption, risk management and oversight in Nigeria. item.title: NEC Endorses 90-Day Economic Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians

item.title: Ministers spend billions to secure appointments, APC spokesman alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently focus on recovering the money. Hassan made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday, describing ministers as among the most corrupt officials in government and claiming the practice predates the APC administration. “Every time a government goes out, the most criminal elements in government are ministers,” he said. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed.” “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he said. “The biggest fraudulent people you arrest after every government are ministers.” He also questioned the role of ministers in budget implementation, arguing that the government’s ability to fund approved budgets should be a priority. “Why do we need ministers? Why do we need budget to be given to ministers?” he asked. ‘Power has improved under Tinubu’ Hassan also defended President Bola Tinubu’s performance, saying the administration had taken steps to address challenges in the power sector. He claimed Tinubu had approved more than ₦4tn for electricity meters, arguing that expanding household metering was important to improving electricity supply. “There is no way you fix power issue without having every household powered,” Hassan said. On the use of solar power at the Presidential Villa, Hassan said the government had introduced financing support to help civil servants acquire solar systems. “That is why he [President Tinubu] introduced Credicorp for civil servants to buy their own solar system,” he said. Tinubu will get votes in the north in 2027 Speaking on the 2027 general election, Hassan argued that President Tinubu’s projects in parts of the North would help him win in states such as Bauchi and Kano, where he lost in the 2023 election. “In 2023, Asiwaju was a candidate and not the president. He’s done a lot in places like Kano and done a lot of streets in the North that will translate to votes,” he said. Hassan also cited the renovation of 287 primary schools and more than 4,000 classrooms through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) as examples of the administration’s achievements. item.description: Thick cables snaked along footpaths in a township outside South Africa’s wealthiest city, Johannesburg, where 180 households have relied on illegal electricity connections for more than 20 years. item.description: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League.
